## Journey Phases / 旅程阶段

> **Guidance** / **指导**：The six phases below are the standard template. Not all phases / 下面的六个阶段是标准模板。不是所有阶段
> apply to all games. A short narrative game may not have Habitual Play or / 都适用于所有游戏。短篇叙事游戏可能没有习惯性游玩或
> Long-Term Engagement. A puzzle game may compress Orientation into First Contact. / 长期参与。解谜游戏可能将定向阶段压缩到首次接触中。
> Delete or merge phases that genuinely do not apply — do not fill them with / 删除或合并真正不适用的阶段——不要用
> placeholder values to make the template look complete. / 占位值来让模板看起来完整。

---

### Phase 1: First Contact (0-5 minutes) / 阶段1：首次接触（0-5分钟）

**Emotional state on arrival** / **到达时的情感状态**: [What is the player feeling before they touch / [玩家在接触游戏前感受如何？
the game? They may be skeptical (purchased on impulse), curious (followed / 他们可能怀疑（冲动购买）、好奇（听从
recommendations), or expectant (been waiting for it). This state is your / 推荐），或期待（一直在等待）。这种状态是你的
starting condition — your design must meet them there.] / 起点条件——你的设计必须在这里与他们相遇。]

**Primary question the player is asking**: [e.g., "Is this worth my time?",
"Will this be too hard?", "Do I understand what I'm supposed to do?"]

**Key experience the game must deliver**:
[What MUST happen in these five minutes for the player to stay? Not a tutorial
beat — an emotional beat. The first contact experience should answer the player's
primary question with a confident "yes." It may be a moment of beauty, a
satisfying mechanical click, a surprising twist on a familiar genre pattern, or
an early win that feels earned.]

**Emotional state on exit**: [What does success look like? e.g., "Curious
about the next layer", "Surprised that this feels different from similar games",
"Already thinking about a decision they made and whether it was right."]

**Risk if this phase fails**: [What does the player do? e.g., "Refund within
the 2-hour Steam window", "Put it down and never return", "Post a negative
first impression", "Recommend it to no one."]

---

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
### Phase 2: Orientation (5-30 minutes) / 阶段2：定向（5-30分钟）

**Emotional state on arrival**: [Player is intrigued but not yet committed.
They are forming their first mental model of what this game is.] / **到达时的情感状态**: [玩家已被吸引但尚未投入。他们正在形成对这款游戏是什么的第一个心理模型。]

**Primary question the player is asking**: [e.g., "How does this actually work?",
"What am I building toward?", "Am I going to be good at this?"] / **玩家在问的主要问题**: [例如："这到底是怎么运作的？"、"我在朝着什么方向前进？"、"我能擅长这个吗？"]

**Key experience the game must deliver**: / **游戏必须交付的关键体验**：
[This is the window where the player builds their foundational mental model.
Describe the one or two "aha" moments that crystallize the game's identity.
The player should feel competence growing — their predictions about the game
should start coming true. They should also catch their first glimpse of depth:
a system or interaction that hints "this goes further than I thought."] / [这是玩家构建他们基础心理模型的窗口。描述一两个让游戏身份变得清晰的"啊哈"时刻。玩家应该感受到能力在增长——他们对游戏的预测应该开始成真。他们也应该第一次瞥见深度：一个暗示"这比我想的更深入"的系统或交互。]

**Emotional state on exit**: [e.g., "Has a working model of the core loop",
"Has made at least one meaningful decision they care about the outcome of",
"Feels the skill ceiling is higher than it first appeared."] / **退出时的情感状态**: [例如："拥有核心循环的运作模型"、"至少做出了一个他们关心结果的有意义决策"、"感觉技能上限比最初看起来更高。"] 

**Risk if this phase fails**: [e.g., "Player concludes the game is shallow",
"Player feels lost and stops trying", "Player never forms a goal."] / **如果此阶段失败的风险**: [例如："玩家认为游戏很肤浅"、"玩家感到迷茫并停止尝试"、"玩家从未形成目标。"]

---

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
### Phase 3: First Mastery (30 minutes - 2 hours) / 阶段3：首次掌握（30分钟-2小时）

**Emotional state on arrival**: [Player understands the basics and is testing
the edges. They are actively trying to get better rather than just trying to
understand.] / **到达时的情感状态**: [玩家理解了基础并在测试边界。他们在积极尝试变得更好，而不仅仅是试图理解。]

**Primary question the player is asking**: [e.g., "What's the right strategy?",
"What's possible if I get good at this?", "What am I missing?"] / **玩家在问的主要问题**: [例如："什么是对的策略？"、"如果我擅长这个，可以做到什么？"、"我错过了什么？"]

**Key experience the game must deliver**: / **游戏必须交付的关键体验**：
[This is the phase where the player earns their first genuine skill victory —
a moment where something that was hard becomes easy through their own growth,
not through the game getting easier. It should feel like crossing a threshold.
They should also discover their first piece of emergent depth: a system
interaction, a build synergy, or a hidden mechanic that rewards curiosity.] / [这是玩家赢得他们第一次真正技能胜利的阶段——一个曾经困难的事情通过他们自己的成长变得容易的时刻，而不是因为游戏变简单了。它应该感觉像跨越了一个门槛。他们也应该发现他们第一次涌现式的深度：一个系统交互、一个构建协同、或者一个奖励好奇心的隐藏机制。]

**Emotional state on exit**: [e.g., "Proud of a specific decision or victory",
"Has an opinion about what the 'right' way to play is (even if wrong)",
"Has questions they want to answer in their next session."] / **退出时的情感状态**: [例如："为某个特定决策或胜利感到自豪"、"对什么是'正确'玩法有看法（即使错了）"、"有他们想在下一次会话中回答的问题。"]

**Risk if this phase fails**: [e.g., "Player never reaches flow state and stops
before the game gets interesting", "Player forms wrong mental model and blames
the game when it breaks."] / **如果此阶段失败的风险**: [例如："玩家从未达到心流状态，在游戏变得有趣之前就停止了"、"玩家形成错误的心理模型，并在它破碎时责怪游戏。"]

---

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
### Phase 4: Depth Discovery (2-10 hours) / 阶段4：深度发现（2-10小时）

**Emotional state on arrival**: [Player has a working strategy and is starting
to see its limits. They are ready to discover that there is more.] / **到达时的情感状态**: [玩家有一个有效的策略并开始看到它的局限。他们准备好发现还有更多。]

**Primary question the player is asking**: [e.g., "Is there a better way?",
"What am I missing that other players know?", "How deep does this actually go?"] / **玩家在问的主要问题**: [例如："有更好的方法吗？"、"我错过了其他玩家知道什么？"、"这到底有多深？"]

**Key experience the game must deliver**: / **游戏必须交付的关键体验**：
[This is where the game's true depth must reveal itself. Players who reach this
phase are your core audience — they have cleared the onboarding and proven their
commitment. They should discover systems, combinations, or strategies that
recontextualize everything they have done so far. The world should feel larger
than the tutorial implied. Design note: Depth Discovery is where many indie
games fail silently. Audit every layer of depth in this window and confirm it
is discoverable without a guide.] / [这是游戏真正深度必须显露的地方。到达这个阶段的玩家是你的核心受众——他们已经通过了入门并证明了他们的投入。他们应该发现重新定义他们迄今为止所做的一切的系统、组合或策略。世界应该感觉比教程暗示的更大。设计注意：深度发现是许多独立游戏默默失败的地方。审核这个窗口中的每一层深度，确认它可以在没有指南的情况下被发现。]

**Emotional state on exit**: [e.g., "Has rebuilt their strategy from scratch
at least once", "Can imagine multiple viable approaches to the same problem",
"Has discovered at least one thing that surprised them."] / **退出时的情感状态**: [例如："至少从头重建了他们的策略一次"、"可以想象对同一问题的多种可行方案"、"至少发现了一件让他们惊讶的事情。"]

**Risk if this phase fails**: [e.g., "Player concludes they have 'finished'
the game and feels mild disappointment", "Player recommends the game but says
'it's a bit short.'"] / **如果此阶段失败的风险**: [例如："玩家认为他们已经'完成'了游戏并感到轻微失望"、"玩家推荐游戏但说'它有点短。'"]

---

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
### Phase 5: Habitual Play (10-50 hours) / 阶段5：习惯性游玩（10-50小时）

> *Note: Not applicable to short-form games. Delete this phase if the game's
> intended experience concludes before this timeframe.* / *注意: 不适用于短篇游戏。如果游戏的预期体验在此时间范围内结束，请删除此阶段。*

**Emotional state on arrival**: [Player considers themselves competent. The
game has become part of their routine. They have a playstyle identity.] / **到达时的情感状态**: [玩家认为自己很熟练。游戏已成为他们日常的一部分。他们有玩法风格身份。]

**Primary question the player is asking**: [e.g., "What's my next goal?",
"Can I beat my previous record?", "What haven't I tried yet?"] / **玩家在问的主要问题**: [例如："我的下一个目标是什么？"、"我能打破我之前的记录吗？"、"我还有什么没尝试过的？"]

**Key experience the game must deliver**: / **游戏必须交付的关键体验**：
[Habitual play requires the game to offer goals beyond the tutorial narrative.
The player generates their own challenges, pursues optional content, or begins
competing. This phase also requires natural session endings that leave forward
tension — the player should always stop with something unfinished that they want
to return to.] / [习惯性游玩要求游戏提供超出教程叙事的目标。玩家产生自己的挑战、追求可选内容或开始竞争。这个阶段还需要留下前进张力的自然会话结束——玩家应该总是带着未完成的事情停下来，这些事情他们想回来继续。]

**Emotional state on exit**: [e.g., "Has a specific goal they are working toward
across multiple sessions", "Considers themselves part of a community of people
who play this game."] / **退出时的情感状态**: [例如："有一个他们跨多个会话正在努力实现的具体目标"、"认为自己属于玩这个游戏的人群社区的一部分。"]

**Risk if this phase fails**: [e.g., "Player churns after completing main content
and never returns", "Game fails word-of-mouth because players don't develop
strong opinions about it."] / **如果此阶段失败的风险**: [例如："玩家在完成主要内容后流失并永不回来"、"游戏口碑失败因为玩家没有对它形成强烈的看法。"]

---

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
### Phase 6: Long-Term Engagement (50+ hours) / 阶段6：长期参与（50小时以上）

> *Note: Only applies to games designed for extended play. Delete this phase if
> it does not fit the game's design intent.* / *注意: 仅适用于设计为长期游玩的游戏。如果它不符合游戏的设计意图，请删除此阶段。*

**Emotional state on arrival**: [Player is a veteran. The game is part of their
identity to some degree. They are invested in the community and the ecosystem.] / **到达时的情感状态**: [玩家是老手。游戏在某种程度上是他们身份的一部分。他们投入了社区和生态系统中。]

**Primary question the player is asking**: [e.g., "What's new?", "Can I reach
the top?", "Can I find something no one has found before?"] / **玩家在问的主要问题**: [例如："有什么新内容？"、"我能达到顶端吗？"、"我能找到以前没有人发现过的东西吗？"]

**Key experience the game must deliver**: / **游戏必须交付的关键体验**：
[Long-term engagement is sustained by different mechanisms than initial fun:
social status, creative expression, competitive standing, or the role of expert
and guide. Design for this phase by asking what role a veteran player wants to
play in the ecosystem.] / [长期参与由不同于初始乐趣的机制维持：社会地位、创意表达、竞争排名，或专家和指导者的角色。通过询问老手玩家想在生态系统中扮演什么角色来设计这个阶段。]

**Emotional state on exit**: [e.g., "Part of a community", "Considered an
expert by newer players", "Invested in the game's ongoing development."] / **退出时的情感状态**: [例如："社区的一部分"、"被新玩家视为专家"、"投入了游戏的持续发展。"]

**Risk if this phase fails**: [e.g., "Veteran players leave and take their
social influence with them, accelerating churn in the broader player base."] / **如果此阶段失败的风险**: [例如："老玩家离开并带走他们的社交影响力，加速更广泛玩家群的流失。"]

## Critical Moments / 关键时刻

> **Guidance**: These are specific, individual events — not phases — that
> must land with precision. A critical moment is a single interaction, scene,
> or beat that carries outsized emotional weight. Missing it can derail the
> entire journey. Identify 8-15 such moments across the game. / **指导**: 这些是具体的单独事件——不是阶段——必须以精确方式命中。关键时刻是带有超常情感重量的单一交互、场景或节拍。错过它可能会使整个旅程脱轨。在整个游戏中识别8-15个这样的时刻。

| Moment | Phase | Emotional Target | If It Fails | 时刻 | 阶段 | 情感目标 | 如果失败 |
|--------|-------|-----------------|-------------|------|------|----------|----------|
| [The first death] | [First Contact] | [Surprise followed by understanding — "I see what I did wrong"] | [Player feels the death was unfair and loses trust in the game's fairness] | [首次死亡] | [首次接触] | [惊讶然后理解——"我看到我做错了什么"] | [玩家感到死亡不公平，失去对游戏公平性的信任] |
| [The first big win] | [Orientation] | [Earned pride — "I figured that out myself"] | [Player feels the win was handed to them and undervalues it] | [首次重大胜利] | [定向] | [赢得的自豪——"我自己弄明白的"] | [玩家感到胜利是白给的，低估了它] |
| [The first system discovery] | [First Mastery] | [Delight — "I didn't know you could do that"] | [Player misses it entirely and never discovers the depth] | [首次系统发现] | [首次掌握] | [欣喜——"我不知道你可以那样做"] | [玩家完全错过，从未发现深度] |
| [The moment the world opens up] | [Depth Discovery] | [Awe followed by hunger — "How much more is there?"] | [Player feels underwhelmed and concludes they have seen everything] | [世界打开的瞬间] | [深度发现] | [敬畏然后是渴望——"还有多少？"] | [玩家感到失望，认为他们已经看完了] |
| [The first endgame goal] | [Habitual Play] | [Renewed purpose — "Now I have something to work toward"] | [Player completes the main content and feels finished] | [首个终局目标] | [习惯性游玩] | [目标重生——"现在我有努力的方向了"] | [玩家完成主要内容，感觉已经结束了] |
| [Add moment] | [Phase] | [Emotional target] | [Failure consequence] | [添加时刻] | [阶段] | [情感目标] | [失败后果] |

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
## Retention Hooks / 留存钩子

> **Guidance**: Retention hooks are the specific mechanisms that pull the player
> back to the next session. They operate at different time scales. A game with
> only one hook type has a fragile retention loop. Strong games layer multiple
> hook types, so players with different motivations all have a reason to return.
> Map each hook to the systems that deliver it — if a hook has no system behind
> it, it is an aspiration, not a design. / **指导**: 留存钩子是拉玩家回到下一次会话的具体机制。它们在不同的时间尺度上运作。只有一种钩子类型的游戏有脆弱的留存循环。强大的游戏分层使用多种钩子类型，使不同动机的玩家都有理由回归。将每个钩子映射到实现它的系统——如果一个钩子背后没有系统支持，它是愿望，而不是设计。

| Hook Type | Hook Description | Systems That Deliver It | 钩子类型 | 钩子描述 | 实现它的系统 |
|-----------|-----------------|------------------------|----------|----------|-------------|
| **Session Start** | [What draws the player in when they launch? e.g., "Unresolved choices from last session", "World state changed", "Daily reward waiting"] | [System names] | **会话开始** | [什么吸引玩家启动游戏？例如："上次会话悬而未决的选择"、"世界状态变化"、"每日奖励等待领取"] | [系统名称] |
| **Session End** | [What feeling do they have as they close the game? e.g., "A goal just out of reach", "A question unanswered", "An upgrade ready to use next time"] | [e.g., "Progress bar at 90%"] | **会话结束** | [他们关闭游戏时有什么感觉？例如："一个就差一点的目标"、"一个未回答的问题"、"一个下次可用的升级"] | [例如："进度条90%"] |
| **Daily Return** | [What reason exists to play today vs. skipping? e.g., "Daily challenge", "Time-gated resource", "Limited-time event"] | [e.g., "Daily quest system"] | **每日回归** | [今天玩而不是放过的理由？例如："每日挑战"、"限时资源"、"限时活动"] | [例如："每日任务系统"] |
| **Long-Term** | [What provides purpose across weeks? e.g., "Season pass milestones", "Competitive ranking reset", "Community challenge goals"] | [e.g., "Ranked system"] | **长期** | [跨周提供目的感的东西？例如："赛季通行证里程碑"、"竞技排名重置"、"社区挑战目标"] | [例如："排位赛系统"] |

## Player Progression Feel / 玩家进度感受

[Describe HOW the player should experience their progression — not the mechanical
system (that belongs in GDDs), but the FEELING of growing. Answer: what is the
primary progression feeling in this game, and what does it concretely look and
feel like at the beginning, middle, and end of the journey?] / [描述玩家应该**如何**体验他们的进度——不是机械系统（那属于GDD），而是成长的感觉。回答：这个游戏中主要的进度感受是什么，它在旅程的开始、中间和结束时具体看起来和感觉是什么样的？]

---

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
## Anti-Patterns to Avoid / 要避免的反模式

> **Guidance**: Anti-patterns are recurring design mistakes that reliably
> break the player journey. List the ones most relevant to this specific game
> and how the design actively guards against them. Be specific. / **指导**: 反模式是可靠地破坏玩家旅程的反复出现的设计错误。列出与这个特定游戏最相关的那些，以及设计如何主动防范它们。要具体。

- **[Player feels punished for experimenting]**: [Example] / **[玩家感到因尝试受到惩罚]**: [示例]
- **[Player loses progress with no explanation]**: [Example] / **[玩家无故失去进度]**: [示例]
- **[Difficulty spike creates a wall, not a gate]**: [Example] / **[难度尖峰创造了一堵墙，而不是一道门]**: [示例]
- **[Player reaches the content ceiling before the emotional arc completes]**: [Example] / **[玩家在情感弧线完成之前就触到了内容天花板]**: [示例]
- **[Mandatory systems are introduced too late]**: [Example] / **[强制性系统引入太晚]**: [示例]
- **[Add anti-pattern specific to this game's design risks]**: [Description] / **[添加针对此游戏设计风险的反模式]**: [描述]

<!-- 中文翻译 -->
## Validation Questions / 验证问题

> **Guidance**: These are questions a playtester session facilitator asks
> during or after a session to verify the journey is working as intended.
> They probe the player's emotional experience and surface gaps between
> design intent and player reality. / **指导**: 这些是测试会话主持人在会话期间或之后问的问题，以验证旅程是否按预期运作。它们探查玩家的情感体验，发现设计意图和玩家现实之间的差距。

**First Contact (0-5 min)** / **首次接触（0-5分钟）**
- [ ] "Without looking at any menus or tooltips, what do you think this game is about?" / "不看任何菜单或提示，你认为这个游戏是关于什么的？"
- [ ] "What's the first thing you want to do next?" / "你接下来第一件想做的事是什么？"

**Orientation (5-30 min)** / **定向（5-30分钟）**
- [ ] "What does winning or succeeding look like to you right now?" / "现在对你来说，胜利或成功是什么样的？"
- [ ] "Is there anything you feel like you should understand but don't?" / "有没有你觉得应该理解但不理解的东西？"

**First Mastery (30 min - 2 hrs)** / **首次掌握（30分钟-2小时）**
- [ ] "What's the best decision you've made so far? Why did you make it?" / "到目前为止你做出的最好决定是什么？你为什么做出这个决定？"
- [ ] "What would you do differently if you started over?" / "如果重新开始，你会有什么不同做法？"

**Depth Discovery (2-10 hrs)** / **深度发现（2-10小时）**
- [ ] "Has the game surprised you? When? How did it feel?" / "游戏令你惊讶了吗？什么时候？感觉如何？"
- [ ] "What questions do you have about systems you haven't fully explored?" / "你对尚未完全探索的系统有什么疑问？"

**Habitual Play (10-50 hrs)** / **习惯性游玩（10-50小时）**
- [ ] "What's your current goal? How long have you been working toward it?" / "你当前的目标是什么？你已经为之努力了多久？"
- [ ] "Have you told anyone about this game? What did you say?" / "你向别人提起过这个游戏吗？你说了什么？"

**General (any phase)** / **通用（任何阶段）**
- [ ] "If you had to stop playing right now, what would you be most eager to
  come back for?" / "如果你现在必须停止游玩，你最渴望回来继续做什么？"
- [ ] "Is there anything you feel the game is not letting you do that you want to do?" / "有没有你觉得游戏不让你做但你想做的事？"
